Clevedon Road crash leaves two in hospital as road remains closed

The road remains closed after a Mini and Land Rover crashed

bristolpost
  • Bookmark
  • Share
News
By
Molly Seaman
  • 18:19, 30 SEP 2026
  • Bookmark

    Two people have been taken to hospital after a serious crash in North Somerset this morning (Wednesday, September 30).

    Emergency services were called to the scene on Clevedon Road in Failand, between its junction with Flax Bourton Road and the B3129 Beggar Bush Lane, at around 8.25am this morning.

    A green Land Rover Defender and a red Mini were involved in the crash and two people suffered injuries and were taken to hospital.

    READ MORE: Two die in A358 lorry crash near Taunton

    READ MORE: Former North Somerset deputy head barred for lesbian sex act comment to female teachers

    At the time of reporting, the driver of the Mini remains in hospital with injuries which are thought to be potentially life-changing.

    The driver of the Land Rover required treatment for injuries but they are not thought to be life-threatening or life-changing.

    The next of kin for both drivers have been located and updated, police confirm.

    Drivers are warned the road is likely to remain closed into this evening.

    An investigation is ongoing and then the vehicles will need to be recovered, officers advised.

    Police are appealing for anyone who witnessed the crash or who has dashcam footage to get in contact with the force.

    A statement from Avon and Somerset Police at 5.30pm said: "Clevedon Road in Failand remains closed between its junction with Flax Bourton Road and the B3129 Beggar Bush Lane following an earlier collision.

    "Officers are keen to hear from anyone with information, dashcam or any other footage which could help their investigations. Please call 101 and give the reference 5226279658."
